newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran condemns German prosecutor over claims.
newsitem.headline: Iran condemns German prosecutor over claims.

text.p: Iran on Monday said a German prosecutor who has accused Iran's spiritual leader of ordering the 1992 killings of three Kurdish dissidents ignored legal principles.
The official Iranian news agency IRNA quoted the head of the judiciary, Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi, as saying the prosecutor "ignored most evident legal principles".

"Ayatollah Yazdi said that based on investigations and legal surveys made by legal experts, there were some mistakes made by the German prosecutor that showed he was under the influence of others," IRNA said.

A senior Iranian cleric last month said Iran would not tolerate the German's prosecutor's claims that Iranian spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other Tehran leaders ordered the political shootings of the Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin.
Iran has denied involvement in the killings.
An Iranian and four Lebanese are on trial for the murders in Berlin's "Mykonos" restaurant in September 1992.
The trial has strained ties between Bonn and Tehran and the accusations against the Iranian leadership have triggered demonstrations at the German embassy in Tehran.
Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and other Iranian government officials have been trying to ease tensions with Germany, the Islamic republic's main trade partner.
